newsitem.title: TURKEY: FOCUS-Turkish shares surge 8 percent on govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Turkish shares surge 8 percent on govt hopes.

text.p: The prospect of Turkey's main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz's forming an "Islamist-free" coalition sent shares soaring eight percent to an all-time closing high on Monday.

Analysts said the market put aside doubts about Yilmaz's ability to muster the necessary parliamentary support for a secularist government in a surge of optimism triggered by his appointment as prime minister-designate late on Friday.
The IMKB National-100 index surged 8.04 percent, or 132 points, to close at a record high 1,774, up from the last record close at 1,700 in January.
Volume jumped to 45.48 trillion lira ($311 million) from 27.12 trillion on Friday, helping the main index break a previous intraday high of 1,751.

"It was clear today how much the stock market longs for a broad-based government. This uptrend will continue until the new government wins a confidence vote," said Ertan Gungor, assistant general manager of Tekstil Investment.
But analysts doubted if gains were sustainable.

"The market is overreacting, but it has good reasons," said Atilla Yesilada, head of reasearch at Global Securities. "It seems they are taking a heavy bet on Yilmaz forming a government, and the bond market is doing the same," he said.
Bond yields continued a sharp decline from highs of 112 percent last week, falling to 100 percent from between 104 and 105 percent on Friday.
Bankers said market participants were ignoring the lack of progress on macro-economic policies in favour of short-term, speculative trading.
"This is technical buying, guided by short-term developments, while no medium- or long-term steps have been taken on the economic front," said a private bank official.
The Turkish lira opened weaker at 146,530 to the dollar from Friday's close of 145,870, but in extremely quiet trade. There was no dealing on the official foreign exchange market.

Yilmaz led a conservative Motherland Party meeting on Monday, confident he could forge a coalition of parties from the left and right to keep out outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists.
Such a bid would need about a dozen MPs' support from rival conservative True Path Party, which under Tansu Ciller is allied with Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Uncertainty over the Yilmaz's level of backing may limit near-term upside potential, brokers said.
"The market will not sustain these levels unless Yilmaz gains the vote of confidence," Yesilada said, adding that it was almost impossible to predict which way the vote would go.
"Whatever happens we are in for a turbulent time going into elections," he said. Yilmaz has said any government he forms would seek elections next spring.
Positive sentiment was reinforced by a weekend resignation of a dissident MP from Ciller's faction in the wake of the president's nomination of Yilmaz.
Islamist Erbakan stepped down last week after months of criticism from the secularist army, which had fuelled political uncertainty and undermined share gains at the start of 1997.
Utility Cukurova Elektrik, state oil refiner Tupras and flat steel maker Eregli led share activity.

"In particular, the movements in Eregli lifted the market as a whole upwards," said Mustafa Toprak of Es Securities. Eregli has a strong impact on the market index because of its high market capitalisation.
($1 = 146,530 Turkish lira)
